message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density (at 25 °C)** | 0.00008988 g cm⁻³ (≈0.0899 kg m⁻³) |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). |
| **Bonding behavior** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂, H₂O, hydrocarbons); can form ionic bonds as H⁺ (proton) or H⁻ (hydride). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (visible/UV/IR). |
| **Magnetic moment** | 1.410 × 10⁻²⁴ J T⁻¹ (electron spin only). |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at constant pressure). |
| **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 20 °C (low). |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air. |
| **Acid–base behavior** | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (forming hydrides). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as H⁻), 0 (as H₂). |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – lowest density, lowest boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive** – readily forms covalent, ionic, and metallic bonds.
- **Key role in life & industry** – water, fuels, acids, bases, and many organic molecules.
- **Isotopic significance** – deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium is radioactive.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
